title: Jordan parts of a probability-measure difference have equal total mass
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $\mu - 
u$ be their signed measure difference. Writing $(\mu-
u)^{+}$ and $(\mu-
u)^{-}$ for the positive and negative parts of the Jordan decomposition of $\mu - 
u$, the two parts assign the same total real mass to the whole space:
\[
(\mu-
u)^{+}(\Omega) = (\mu-
u)^{-}(\Omega).
\]
replaced:
For probability measures $\mu$ and $
u$, the Jordan positive part and the Jordan
negative part of $\mu - 
u$ assign equal real mass to $\Omega$:
$((\mu-
u)^+)(\Omega) = ((\mu-
u)^-)(\Omega)$.
